topic: Software factories and execution trace analysis

components.title: Execution traces in software factories
components.teaches: Students learn what execution traces are, how coding agents emit them during iterative loop engineering, and why they are essential for diagnosing failures in software factories.

components.title: Log structure and iteration markers
components.teaches: Students examine the standardized format of iterative development logs, including timestamps, iteration IDs, tool calls, and error markers, enabling systematic navigation of up to 2000 lines.

components.title: Typical failure patterns in agent traces
components.teaches: Students identify three recurring failure categories—environment misconfiguration, dependency resolution errors, and logic regressions—and learn the trace signatures that distinguish each.

components.title: Trace collection and parsing tooling
components.teaches: Students watch a live demonstration of the factory's trace collector, log aggregator, and a Python script that parses raw logs into structured JSON for analysis.

components.title: Worked example: environment misconfiguration
components.teaches: Students follow a step‑by‑step analysis of a 500‑line trace, locating missing environment variables, correlating error codes, and citing exact log lines as evidence for the first failure cause.

components.title: Worked example: dependency resolution failure
components.teaches: Students trace a version conflict across iterations, observe repeated fetch retries, and extract the specific dependency graph lines that prove the second failure cause.

components.title: Worked example: logic regression detection
components.teaches: Students compare successive iteration outputs, spot a behavioral change in test results, and pinpoint the commit diff lines that constitute the third failure cause with supporting log excerpts.

components.title: Comparing failure causes across traces
components.teaches: Students contrast the three failure signatures side‑by‑side, evaluate their frequency and impact, and practice ranking them by severity using a structured rubric.

components.title: Activity: analyze full 2000‑line log
components.teaches: In pairs, students receive a 2000‑line factory log, apply the parsing script, identify at least three distinct failure causes, and record supporting log line numbers for each.

components.title: Discussion: reporting and best practices
components.teaches: Students present their findings, critique evidence quality, discuss how to automate failure‑cause detection, and outline a checklist for future trace analyses.

video.description:
Luciq (formerly Instabug) | A practical guide to using execution traces to diagnose performance issues in your mobile app.

Execution traces show you exactly what your app is doing at a code level during a slow or failing session. In this video, we walk through how to read and use execution traces inside Luciq to get to the root cause faster.

Luciq is the pioneer of Agentic Mobile Observability. Formerly known as Instabug, Luciq's AI agents proactively detect, diagnose, and resolve mobile app issues before they reach users.

Learn more: https://luciq.ai
Book a demo: https://luciq.ai/request-demo
